title: Anupama Ramachandran retains world women's snooker title in Indore
dek: The Indian beat Hong Kong's So Man Yan 3-1 in the IBSF final for her second successive world title.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Anupama Ramachandran retained her IBSF World Women's Snooker Championship title on Saturday, beating Hong Kong's So Man Yan 3-1 in the final in Indore, Madhya Pradesh.

She lost the opening frame 16-58 but took the next three to win her second world title in a row, according to reports. Last year she became the first Indian woman to win the IBSF world snooker title.

On the way to the final she beat fellow Indian Keerthana Pandian 3-1 and England's Tessa Davidson 3-1, reports said. The championship, run by the International Billiards and Snooker Federation for amateur players, was played in India this year, giving her the advantage of a home crowd.

India has a long record in the federation's world championships, especially in billiards, but women's snooker titles have been rare.

In other sport on Saturday, India's women beat Thailand 7-0 in the Women's Asian Champions Trophy hockey in Bhopal, with Deepika scoring a hat-trick, according to reports.
